newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Great Eagle up on strong earnings report.
newsitem.headline: Great Eagle up on strong earnings report.

text.p: Shares of Great Eagle Holdings Ltd rose on Thursday after the company reported higher than expected yearly earnings and on hopes of stronger earnings stemming from the possible spinoff of a unit, brokers said.
Great Eagle shares were up HK$0.90 to HK$34.90 in mid-morning trade on volume of 391,400 shares.
"Strong earnings plus hope of a possible spinoff later this year, particularly in this favourable market sentiment, fuelled buying," said Anthony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The property group on Wednesday reported a 28.7 percent rise in profit for the year to September 30, 1996, to HK$1.06 billion, up from analysts' consensus forecast of 23 percent.
"The results were very good. It is not overpriced now," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities, adding that Great Eagle's net asset value per share was about HK$44.58.
In August, Great Eagle said it was considering the listing of shares of a new holding company containing its office and commercial property interests.
Brokers said a big trading discount to its net asset value (NAV) also aided buying.
Frederick Tsang, head of research at PrimeEast Securities, said Great Eagle was trading at a discount of about 21 percent to its NAV, which he put at HK$44.63 per share.
"Office prices have gone up quite a bit this year so probably next year or in the current year we might see NAV figures higher than HK$44.60," Tsang said.
